newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: SOCCER-UAE BEAT IRAQ WITH DRAMATIC "GOLDEN GOAL".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UAE BEAT IRAQ WITH DRAMATIC "GOLDEN GOAL".

text.p: Defender Abdel Hussain scored a "golden goal" with a free kick from 30 metres to give hosts the United Arab Emirates a 1-0 victory over Iraq in an Asian Cup quarter-final tie on Sunday.
Hussain crashed the ball home 13 minutes into sudden death extra time after a goalless 90 minutes.

The goal, which immediately brought the match to a halt, set most of the 50,000 spectators dancing with joy while motorists listening to commentary on radios across the country honked their horns in celebration.
The Iraqi players, who had dominated much of the game, sank to their knees.
The UAE could have won the match in normal time from the penalty spot after Iraqi defender Abdul Jabar Hanoon was penalised for bringing down Hassan Ahmed in the 58th minute.
But midfielder Bakhit Saad's spot-kick was weak and Iraqi keeper Emad Hassan, diving to his right, made the save.

Iraq generally had the better of the match. Striker Laith Shihaib hit the woodwork with a strike from 20 metres in the first half and four minutes later Husam Naji shot across goal instead of into an empty net after UAE keeper Muhsin Fairouz fumbled a save.
But the home team survived and won the match in dramatic fashion.
Under the golden goal rule, the first goal scored in extra time clinches the match for the scorer's team. The game ends as soon as the goal is scored.
The UAE now play either Kuwait or defending champions Japan, who meet in the second quarter-final later on Sunday.

UAE - 17-Muhsin Fairouz; 2-Abdel Hussain; 3-Munther Abdullah; 6-Ismail Ismail; 7-Bakhit Saad; 10-Adnan Al Talyani (11-Zuhair Bkhait 46); 12-Hassan Mubarak; 13-Abdulaziz Mohamed (14-Khamis Saad 91); 16-Hassan Ahmed; 18-Ahmed Ahmed; 23-Adel Ahmed (19-Ali Ghawas 36).

Iraq - 1-Emad Hassan; 2-Samir Hassan; 3-Walid Afat; 4-Abdul Jabar Hanoon; 5-Radhi Swadi; 6-Esam Salem (9-Ali Shaniyn 86); 7- Khalid Sabbar; 10-Qahtan Drain (19-Ahmad Karin 79); 12-Hayder Majeed; 15-Husam Naji; 17-Laith Shihaib.
